clue.text: State capital no great thing, house overlooking it

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece overlooking another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: taken as written
a lulu is an outstanding or remarkable thing

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a state capital, with some house looking down over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No great thing' reads as a put-down of the city, but it is wordplay: 'no' kept as written plus slang for a remarkable thing. In a down clue 'overlooking' puts the house piece on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital city of the US state of Hawaii, an example of a state capital.

clue.text: Rare phenomenon, very rare to idle about

parts.note: a steak cooked very rare, barely seared, is called blue
to moon about is to drift around aimlessly, idling

explanation.surface: Someone seldom seen loafing around is called a rare sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very rare' is steak language, not frequency: a blue steak is cooked even less than rare.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening once in a blue moon is very infrequent, so the phrase names a rare occurrence.

clue.text: Successful investor in 11? Then capital in tomatoes!

parts.note: 11 across is rabbit food, and a buffet laid on in a rabbit ... would be a spread of it, a ... buffet

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, in the word tomatoes is wanted

explanation.surface: A whimsical image of rabbits feasting on salad, then tomatoes topping the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: The '11' cross-reference points to RABBIT FOOD: where it is served in a warren is a WARREN BUFFET. The first letter of 'tomatoes', from 'capital in', finishes the investor's surname with its double T.
explanation.definitionFit: Warren Buffett, the American head of Berkshire Hathaway, is famed as one of history's most successful investors.

clue.text: Recovery when hit by the Beatles

definitions.meaning: recovering something, retrieving what was lost
a 1969 number-one single by the Beatles

explanation.surface: A comeback that happens when the Beatles strike a chart blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a blow received, but it is a chart success: the Beatles' 1969 single.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrieve or regain is to recover, so retrieval is a recovery; the second sense is the song title itself.

clue.text: One plays this G & S character

definitions.meaning: the solitaire card game, played by one person alone
the milkmaid heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera of 1881

explanation.surface: A performer taking a part in a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One plays this' suggests an actor in a role; it means the card game played by one person. G & S is Gilbert and Sullivan, the Victorian comic-opera partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game for a single player is called this in Britain, and it is also the title character of a Gilbert and Sullivan opera.

clue.text: Sweaty hands, signs of discomfort in woman

parts.note: feeling sweaty means feeling hot
in poker, flushes are hands of five cards in one suit

explanation.surface: Clammy palms betraying a woman's unease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' looks like palms, but it means poker hands: flushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden waves of heat and redness are a common symptom for women going through the menopause.

clue.text: A short type of clue

parts.note: being short with someone is being cross, curt and irritable

explanation.surface: Talk of a brief kind of crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' looks like it describes the clue's length, but it means cross, as in short-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword clues are divided into those read horizontally and those read vertically; this names the horizontal kind.

clue.text: China in Korea, say — one's ideal partner?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: china is a mate, from cockney rhyming slang china plate; a mate in Korea's capital would be a Seoul mate

explanation.surface: Porcelain found in Korea pitched as the perfect partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country or porcelain but a pal, from rhyming slang (china plate = mate). Seoul is Korea's capital; Seoul mate is heard the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person ideally suited to someone, often as a romantic partner, is called this.

clue.text: A lot came to be evacuated immediately

parts.note: tons of something is a lot of it

indicators.note: the word came is emptied of its middle letters, leaving its outside pair

explanation.surface: A crowd arrived only to be cleared out without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evacuated' empties 'came' to its outer letters, C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without delay, straight away, is doing it this way; a plain synonym.

clue.text: See 22
Too bad, if starters in restaurant burnt beyond recognition — there's salad!

indicators.note: these letters are changed past recognising, like burnt food, so they are rearranged
the first letters, the starters, of the words restaurant and burnt are taken

explanation.surface: A diner complains the restaurant's starters were charred, and all they got was salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters in' gives R and B from 'restaurant burnt'; with TOOBADIF these are rearranged, signalled by 'beyond recognition'.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad is dismissively called food fit for rabbits, a jokey idiom for green leaves.

clue.text: Sound of bagpipes that's hard to bear!

definitions.meaning: the drone of bagpipes, or a refrain
a heavy load or trouble that is difficult to carry

explanation.surface: A grumble that the noise of bagpipes is unbearable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' plays on carrying a load as well as putting up with a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A load or responsibility hard to carry is one sense; an old sense names a drone or refrain in music, as in bagpipes.

clue.text: Redraft in decree outlining very strong argument

indicators.note: the reordered letters outline, or surround, the other piece
to redraft is to rewrite, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud or strong

explanation.surface: Rewording part of a court order around a forceful case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redraft' rearranges IN DECREE into DIERENCE; 'outlining' wraps it around FF, the music marking fortissimo.
explanation.definitionFit: A difference, as in a difference of opinion, is a quarrel or disagreement, so it can mean an argument.

clue.text: Policeman not able to claim that Spanish victory

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so the shortened policeman holds the other piece
not removes the word able from the policeman

parts.note: a constable is a police officer of the lowest rank
taken as written
que is Spanish for that

explanation.surface: An officer unable to take credit for a Spanish triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Policeman not able' looks like a description of an incompetent officer, but 'not' removes the word 'able' from the full rank; 'to claim' then wraps what is left around the Spanish word.
explanation.definitionFit: A conquest is a triumph won by force, so it is a kind of victory; a plain synonym.

clue.text: See 3
Flashy and cheap little houses to auction off

indicators.note: houses here is a verb, meaning holds inside

parts.note: something little is tiny
auctioning off goods is selling them

explanation.surface: Gaudy cheap cottages being put under the hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun about property but is a verb: TINY houses SELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinsel is glittering and cheap, so anything like it is showy but tawdry.

clue.text: Hot spring turned on for every one, possibly

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece on another follows it

parts.note: per means for each
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: turned means the word for spring is read backwards

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A hot spring switched on for everyone to use, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses only the spring, giving APS; in an across clue 'on' places the hot-plus-spring part after the 'for every one' piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something may be so, without certainty, is a plain synonym for maybe.

clue.text: Criminal person, one inside, ending in slammer

definitions.text: Criminal person, one inside, ending in slammer

indicators.note: one goes inside the jumbled letters
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters of person are bent out of order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the ending, the last letter, of the word slammer is taken

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker, locked up, finishing up in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' jumbles PERSON to PRSONE; 'inside' puts I in, and 'ending in' adds R from slammer. The whole clue describes the answer, a crook ending up in the slammer, slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held in jail after conviction is a convict; the whole clue paints one.

clue.text: Finding scorer, cup ties both kicking off

parts.note: Verdi, the Italian opera composer, wrote scores

indicators.note: the first letters, kick-offs, of both cup and ties are taken

explanation.surface: A goalscorer discovered in a pair of cup matches starting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' suggests football but means a composer who writes scores; 'kicking off' takes C and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A jury's verdict is its finding, the decision it reaches on the facts.

clue.text: Queen inside volcano should be brought back, they feel

indicators.note: brought back means the combined letters are read in reverse
the queen goes inside the volcano's name

parts.note: Etna is the volcano on Sicily
Anne was Queen of Great Britain from 1702 to 1714

explanation.surface: A royal trapped in a volcano who must be rescued, they think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts the queen within the Sicilian volcano, giving EANNETNA; 'brought back' then reverses the whole string. 'they feel' is the definition, not an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects use their feelers to touch and sense things, so these are things that feel.

clue.text: Apple inferior to an unspecified number — more in apple-pie order?

indicators.note: in a down clue a piece inferior to another sits below it, so comes after

parts.note: N is used in maths for an unspecified number
an eater is a dessert apple, eaten raw rather than cooked

explanation.surface: An apple ranked below some number, in a tidier arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple' is EATER, an apple for eating raw; it sits under N.
explanation.definitionFit: Apple-pie order means perfect tidiness, so more in it is tidier.

clue.text: Molière requires three seconds to contrive a comparatively oxymoronic theatrical cliché?

indicators.note: to contrive is to devise or put together, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the French comic playwright, whose name gives its letters
s is the abbreviation for second, so three of them give three s letters

explanation.surface: A French playwright needing three seconds to produce a stage cliché built on contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to contrive' reorders MOLIERE plus SSS. 'comparatively oxymoronic' points to the two comparatives that seem to contradict one another.
explanation.definitionFit: This maxim of minimalism pairs two opposite comparatives, so it sounds self-contradictory, and is an overused saying in stage design.

clue.text: Half a century, one counting as a run

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, half of a hundred
an adder is one who adds up, counting

explanation.surface: A batter's fifty, one of them counted as a run.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket misleads: a century is a hundred runs, but here only L, fifty in Roman numerals, is wanted. A ladder is a run in stockings or tights, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical split in stockings or tights is called a ladder in Britain and a run in America.

clue.text: Spooner's locks implanted, nothing on top

indicators.note: Spooner's signals swapping the opening sounds of two words

parts.note: locks of the head are hair
hair with beads set in it is beaded

explanation.surface: Hair transplanted onto a scalp with nothing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the first sounds of HAIR BEADED gives BARE HEADED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without a hat means having no covering on your head.

clue.text: See 2
Low tide initially doubtful

parts.note: to low is to make the sound of cattle, a moo

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word tide

explanation.surface: A low tide, at first uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective for the tide but is a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A moot point is open to debate and unsettled, so moot means uncertain.

clue.text: Intoxicating drink making camels woozy

indicators.note: woozy means dizzy and unsteady, so the letters of camels stagger out of order

explanation.surface: A drink so strong it leaves camels dizzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woozy' rearranges CAMELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mescal is a Mexican spirit distilled from agave, a strong alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Consider putting cut inside lid

indicators.note: the cut goes inside the lid

parts.note: a lid is a cover
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: Instructions to place a slit inside a lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting' is only a link; 'inside' signals the container, with the axe-chopping verb going into the lid's synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder something at length is to mull it, a figurative idiom from chewing food.
